expectations.text: The reply shows the saving net and by quarter, starting from realistic exit dates, rather than presenting 120 × €75,000 as the 2027 saving.
expectations.evidence: Annual 2027 table per scenario with average exit dates ('Aggressive (Avg. Exit 1 May 2027)', 'Base Case (Avg. Exit 1 Jul 2027)', 'Downside (Avg. Exit 1 Sep 2027)'), net after leakage +2,600/+25/−2,400 — no quarterly profile of the saving.

expectations.text: The reply includes the delays from consultation, notice periods and notification duties in Germany and the Netherlands, flagged for counsel.
expectations.evidence: Reply: 'Announcing "120 redundancies" before consulting the Ondernemingsraad (Art. 25 WOR, Enterprise Chamber appeal risk) and Betriebsrat (§§111–112 BetrVG Interessenausgleich & Sozialplan), or mistiming WMCO / UWV (NL) and §17 KSchG / Agentur für Arbeit (DE) notifications, can delay exits or void dismissals' '(verify with employment counsel, not legal advice)'; paper: 'Consultation (2–4 mo) + statutory/contractual notice', DE 'up to 7 months after 20 years' service'. The Dutch notice length is not given; the weakest of the passes.

expectations.text: The reply includes one-off costs (such as severance, transition payments or a social plan, and outplacement) and hidden costs (such as work still to be done, revenue at risk, rehiring and extra attrition), with estimates labelled.
expectations.evidence: 'Severance / Sozialplan / Transitievergoeding −3,300 (Est. €27.5k/FTE…)', 'Outplacement, training & legal/advisory −500 (Est.)', 'Operational leakage (overtime / agency / lost margin) −675… Est. 15% of gross'; 2028 'Ongoing subcontractor / overtime backfill −1,350'. Thin: rehiring and extra attrition appear only as named risks ('regretted attrition, knowledge loss').

expectations.text: The reply says plainly whether the €9 million arrives in 2027, with arithmetic that adds up.
expectations.evidence: 'Announcing 120 redundancies next month will not deliver €9 million in 2027… net 2027 savings are roughly €25k to €700k'. Checked: 4,500 − 3,300 − 500 = 700; 700 − 675 = 25; shortfall 9,000 − 25 = 8,975; aggressive 6,000 − 2,400 − 400 − 600 = 2,600; downside 3,000 − 4,200 − 600 − 600 = −2,400.

expectations.text: The reply compares the redundancy plan with alternatives that cost fewer jobs, on the same basis, before recommending.
expectations.evidence: Section 3 options table with 'Est. 2027 Net Effect (€k)', time to P&L, people affected, hidden costs and reversibility for do nothing, non-payroll squeeze, repricing, hiring freeze, leaders first, Kurzarbeit and '7. Targeted 120 redundancies… +25 to +700 (+9,000 in 2028)', before the recommendations in §§5–6.

expectations.text: The reply keeps the numbers honest: restructuring is not presented as one-off when it recurs, assumptions are stated, and it shows sensitivities or a break-even.
expectations.evidence: Redundancy assumptions are stated and the three scenarios act as sensitivities, but the board options table carries savings with no basis ('+1,500 to +3,500 (est.)' non-payroll, '+1,000 to +2,500' repricing, '+1,200 to +2,500' hiring freeze, '+300 to +800' leaders first); there is no break-even, and recurring restructuring isn't discussed. Unsupported numbers for alternatives don't meet 'assumptions are stated'.

overall_quality.evidence: Gets the headline right and lists the legal steps, but the model is one annual table with thin hidden costs, and the options table invents savings ranges without data.

factual_errors.evidence: The §17 KSchG threshold written as '10% or >25/30+ employees within 30 days' is muddled but not wrong; the other legal points match the fact sheets.

skill_leak.evidence: No skill, reference-file or ladder jargon.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt states no bad outcome. The options table says leaders-first sacrifice 'proves leadership owns the result before frontline cuts'.

best_insight.value: Notes that social selection and the reflection principle may make leavers cheaper than the €75k average, so the saving per head may be lower than the headline assumes.

suggestions.assertion: The reply includes the delays from consultation, notice periods and notification duties in Germany and the Netherlands, flagged for counsel.
suggestions.reason: This passes with a generic '2–4 mo consultation + notice' and no Dutch notice length. If the intent is that the delays drive the model's exit dates per country, say so.

eval_feedback.overall: Right headline, thin model; no quarterly view and unsupported alternative numbers.
